name: Methionine
info: Contains sulfur in a thioether. Unlike cysteine, it does not form disulfide bridges.

history.clue: The name abbreviates a description of its methyl-containing sulfur fragment.
history.story: In 1921, John Howard Mueller isolated a new sulfur-containing amino acid from casein. In 1928, Barger and Coyne established its structure and proposed the name “methionine.” It abbreviates a description of the –S–CH₃ fragment: “meth-” refers to methyl, while “thio-” refers to sulfur.
